# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup (main+0x493300) hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as virtual address memory

# and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize, as Patrick's Parabox (the same Unity 2020.3.30f1). The node area cut for this sdk build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) shrinks the AddressRegionManager's node area to 62 MB.
# With the hardware pool (3.2 GB) StandardAllocator's 1 GB-aligned region and Unity's own regions used the alias region up to +4.26 GB of 4.38 in the first 5 s (the NSP script's heap check).
# So Ace Attorney Investigations Collection's layout: a 1 GB pool and the 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region).
# Measured on the Mac over 15 minutes from boot through a new game into the first investigation (probes on VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion's success path sdk+0x37c2a0 and
# FreeAddressRegion sdk+0x37caf8, commits from the DM_SVC map log): StandardAllocator takes 960 MB at +64 MB and commits 0.29 GB of it; Unity's allocator (main+0x484024) holds about
# 1.10 GB in 170 regions (16.25 MB and 2.25 MB blocks, created and freed as scenes load), 1.03 GB of it mapped; 2.1 GB of regions live in all, 1.26 GB mapped, 1.96 GB resident.
# The highest region end climbs (+3.77 GB after 7 minutes) while the live total stays flat: the SDK places each region at the bottom of the highest gap that fits (sdk+0x37c2d0 walks
# the gaps from the top down), so new regions go above the highest live one until the top is used and only then into the holes below
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
